Master Direction on Incentives for Currency Distribution and Exchange and Penalties / Penal Provisions for Bank Branches and Currency Chests for Deficiency in Rendering Customer Service and Reporting of Transactions / Balances RBI has formulated a Scheme of incentives to encourage banks for setting up requisite Currency Chest (CC) infrastructure and facilitating distribution / exchange of notes and coins. Further, the RBI has also prescribed a Scheme of penal interest/penalties in order to ensure accurate and timely reporting of CC transactions and provision of proper customer service to the members of public by CCs/branches/ATMs of banks.

# Page 4^page=4
Master Direction on Incentives and penal provisions for bank branches and CCs in respect of currency operations. In order to ensure that all bank branches provide proper customer service, the Bank has formulated a Scheme of Penalties for bank branches including CCs, for deficiency in rendering customer service to the members of public.

# Page 5^page=5
Small Finance Banks (up to two years from the commencement of their banking business) and Payment Banks may exchange mutilated and imperfect notes at their option.

# Page 6^page=6
Banks and White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) are required to submit system- generated statements regarding ATM downtime caused due to non-replenishment of cash. This reporting is applicable only for those ATMs where cash-out exceeds 10 hours in a month, and the total downtime hours must be mentioned. These statements must be submitted to the concerned RBI Issue Office under whose jurisdiction the ATMs are located, within five days of the following month.

# Page 12^page=12
Penal Provisions for Reporting of Transactions/ Balances at CCs - Reporting Procedure Minimum Transaction Amount - The minimum amount of deposit into / withdrawal from CC shall be ₹50,000/-and thereafter, in multiples of ₹10,000/-. Reporting Timelines - The CCs shall invariably report all transactions through CyM-CC portal on the same day by 7 pm. CCs reporting in CyM on Sundays or Holidays – In case CyM CC portal is available on the day a specific CC is permitted to operate (i.e. on a local holiday), the CC shall report the transactions in CyM on the same day by 7 PM. In case CyM-CC portal is not available on the said day (i.e. on a global holiday/ 2nd or 4th Saturdays of the month/ Sunday), the CC shall report denomination-wise consolidated deposit and/ or withdrawal amount and denomination-wise chest closing balance of the day by 7 pm to the concerned Issue Office of RBI by e-mail and report day’s transactions in CyM on the next working day.

# Page 13^page=13
Penal Provisions for Reporting of Transactions/ Balances at CCs - Reporting Procedure Under the Business Continuity Plan (BCP), the RBI allows flexibility in using the CyM-CC portal to ensure uninterrupted reporting by CCs. If a CC faces connectivity or technical issues, the bank’s Back Office (BO) Administrator can temporarily map the user ID of another CC within the same bank to carry out transactions on its behalf. Once the transactions are completed, access rights must be restored to the original CC. This mechanism helps avoid delays in reporting and prevents punitive action. Banks must maintain proper records of such temporary authorizations for audit purposes and include this arrangement in their BCP. Relaxation in reporting timelines during strike situations may be granted on a case-by-case basis.

# Page 14^page=14
Penal Provisions for Reporting of Transactions/ Balances at CCs - Levy of Penal interest

# Page 15^page=15
Penal Provisions for Reporting of Transactions/ Balances at CCs - Levy of Penalty Soiled note remittances sent to RBI shall not be shown as withdrawal by CCs and in case of such reporting penalty shall be levied. Reporting of Diversions - All CC diversions (both between CCs of the same bank and between CCs of different banks) have to be reported through the ‘Diversion Module’ of CyM-CC Portal. The CC sending the diversion should initiate the entry and the receiving CC should acknowledge the same. Diversions should not be reported as deposit / withdrawal and in case of any such wrong reporting penalty shall be levied. Delayed reporting where CCs had ‘Net Deposit’ - For delayed reporting of instances where CCs had reported ‘net deposit’, penal interest shall not be charged. However, to ensure discipline in reporting of CC transaction, a flat penalty shall be levied for such delayed reporting.

# Page 16^page=16
Operational Guidelines on Levy of Penalty / Penal Interest Competent Authority - The Officer-in-Charge of the Issue Department of Regional Office under whose jurisdiction the defaulting CC / bank branch / ATM is located is the competent authority to determine the nature of the irregularity and impose the applicable penalty. Appellate Authority - The Controlling Office of the Currency Chest or bank branch may appeal against the decision of the Competent Authority to the Regional Director / Chief General Manager / Officer-in-Charge of the Regional Office concerned within 1 month from the date of debit or imposition of penalty. Representations, if any, on account of genuine difficulties faced by CCs especially in hilly/ remote areas and those affected by natural calamities, etc., may be made to the appellate authority. Appeals for waiver of penalty made on grounds such as staff being new/ untrained, lack of awareness, corrective action having been taken/ shall be taken, etc., shall not be considered.

# Page 17^page=17
Q1. Consider the following statements regarding penalties for deficiency in customer service: 1. A penalty of ₹10,000 per instance is imposed for deficiency in customer service. 2. A penalty of ₹5 lakh is imposed if there are more than 5 instances in a year. 3. Penalty is imposed only if ATM remains out of cash for more than 24 hours in a month. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? A. 1 only B. 1 and 2 only C. 2 and 3 only D. 1 and 3 only E. 1, 2 and 3 MCQs for Practice
